The prior version (2026-07-01) used 1.09; the RMB has appreciated ~7% against the HKD/USD since, which is also the source of BYD's FX finance-cost losses. inputs.wacc_rationale: Single 10.0% CNY WACC for all three scenarios (adaptations 7f: risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates -- the prior 10/11/12% split charged risk twice). Built in the flows' currency: China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta 1.25 (cyclical auto, high operating leverage, price war) x 6.5% ERP for Chinese equities (incl. country premium) = 10.0% cost of equity; net debt is ~nil on the broad definition, so WACC ~ CoE.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB 8,610m (30-Jun-2026) are in total_debt; no lease charge in the flows (lease_cost_pct_path 0). ROU depreciation (~RMB 2.7bn/yr) sits inside D&A; ROU additions are non-cash and small (RMB 1.7bn FY2025).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (incl. BYD Electronic, 0285.HK, ~65.8% owned). NCI charged ONCE in the bridge at MARKET value of the ~34.2% BYDE minority: 0285.HK HKD 23.16 (2026-10-09) x ~2,253m shares = HKD 52.2bn x 34.2% = HKD 17.85bn = RMB 15,230m. Book NCI is RMB 12,552m. FY2025 tie-out: modelled EBIT ex finance/investment income RMB 36.7bn x (1-15%) + ~RMB 3bn net investment/finance income ~ RMB 34bn vs total net profit 33.8bn / attributable 32.6bn.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 interim, unaudited). Debt: short-term borrowings 37,646 + non-current liabilities due within one year 3,453 + long-term borrowings 61,201 + bonds payable 14,994 (= CSV TotalDebt 117,294) + lease liabilities 8,610 = 125,904. Cash: cash & equivalents 55,619 (monetary funds 58,738 less restricted) + financial assets held for trading 69,940 (liquid wealth-management/treasury products) = 125,559. Net debt +345 (essentially nil). RECONCILIATION: narrow cash-minus-borrowings is RMB -61.7bn net debt; the RMB 69.9bn trading portfolio closes the gap. At Dec-2025 the same definition gave +RMB 10.1bn net cash; the swing is H1 working-capital build (inventories +RMB 51.6bn) and the RMB 17bn perpetual bond redemption, partly funded by a RMB 10bn bond issue.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (routing: non-US cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; matches the prior owner-FCF model family for this ticker). CHANGED from the 2026-07-01 version: (1) 5-year 'OCF margin minus capex' FCF-margin build replaced by the house component build (EBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> cash tax -> capex -> working capital) over 10 years, because the year-5 margin was still ramping; (2) per-scenario WACC 10/11/12% replaced by one 10% CNY WACC; (3) equity bridge now adds the investment assets whose income is excluded from EBIT (matching-asset rule) and deducts the RMB 20.8bn perpetual bonds that sit in equity. EBITDA is defined as operating profit EXCLUDING finance expenses/income (incl. FX gains/losses) and investment income, plus D&A, plus SBC; government grants/VAT super-deduction 'other income' (RMB 13.8bn FY2025, ~1.7% of revenue) is left inside EBITDA. Actuals on that definition: FY2024 EBITDA ~15.1%, FY2025 ~14.7% (EBIT 36.7bn + D&A 80.5bn + SBC 0.9bn), H1 2025 ~13.8%, H1 2026 ~17.4% (EBIT 20.0bn + D&A 39.2bn + SBC 0.6bn on 344.8bn). Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC; interest income NOT stripped because net cash is ~nil and finance income is outside EBIT. Buybacks: FY2025 RMB 3,988m A-share repurchase was for the employee share plan, not a capital return. Year 1 = FY2026 and is discounted a full year from the valuation date although 9 months have elapsed (slightly conservative); the H1 2026 owner FCF already reflected in the 30-Jun balance sheet is added back in the bridge so H1 is not counted twice.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (30.4% 3yr) runs ~28% above revenue (23.8%) and ~21% above split-adjusted EPS (25.2%): equity was inflated by the USD 5.6bn H-share placing (Mar-2025) and perpetual-bond issuance. Neither historical rate is forward-replicable at RMB 800bn revenue: FY2025 revenue +3.5%, H1 2026 -7.1%.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr); EPS split-adjusted by 9,117.2/2,911.1 = 3.132. Owner-FCF CAGRs not calculable: owner FCF FY2025 is RMB -98.6bn (reported -97.7bn less SBC 0.9bn) after RMB 156.8bn capex; best-ever reported FCF margin 4.6% (FY2024). SBC is ~0.1-0.2% of revenue, so the SBC adjustment barely moves the series. Selected growth = 10-year revenue CAGR of the base path, not a historical rate.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 flat: H1 revenue -7.1% (RMB 344.8bn) and H2 2025 base RMB 432.7bn; September global units +17% YoY and overseas +154% YoY support H2 ~+5%, giving FY2026 ~RMB 800bn. The prior +10% FY2026 path is no longer reachable. FY2027-28 +8%: overseas target >2.5m units (from 1.9-2.0m) at higher ASPs, domestic stabilising off a -33% base; decelerating to 3% as the overseas ramp matures.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA 16.0% FY2026 (H1 17.4% on the house definition, H2 heavier on lower-margin domestic volume), easing to 14.0% as D&A intensity falls and the advanced-manufacturing VAT super-deduction (inside 'other income', ~1.7% of revenue) lapses after 2027. Implied EBIT 5.3% FY2026 -> 5.9% mature, vs 6.4% FY2024 peak and 4.6% FY2025.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 12.5% of revenue FY2026 (H1 13.0%, RMB 44.7bn) after the FY2025 19.5% peak, tapering to 8.5% as Hungary/Turkey/Brazil/Thailand plants and the 20,000 FLASH charging stations complete. D&A ~10% now (FY2025 RMB 80.5bn incl. long-term deferred amortisation; H1 2026 RMB 39.2bn) falls to 8.0% as the short-lived 2022-25 asset base rolls off; terminal capex/D&A 1.06x for 2.5% growth.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 25% FY2026: current tax is running far above the book charge (H1 2026 current tax RMB 5.96bn on RMB 14.6bn profit before tax) because intra-group export profits are taxed in China before overseas sale and overseas start-up losses cannot be offset (DTA for unrealised intra-group profit RMB 24bn and tax losses RMB 14bn at FY2025). Settles at 20%: 15% HNTE rate in China blended with ~20-25% overseas as mix passes 40%.
base.wc_rationale: Zero: BYD runs negative working capital (trade+bills payables RMB 230bn + contract liabilities 80bn vs inventory 190bn + receivables 60bn at Jun-2026), but the 2025 60-day supplier-payment pledge is unwinding the float (FY2025 payables -RMB 37bn). Growth neither funds nor consumes cash in the base.

bull.rationale: Overseas hits 2.0m units FY2026 and >2.5m FY2027 with Hungary in series production, sidestepping the EU BEV tariff; premium brands (12.8% of mix, +61%) and BESS lift margins; Q2 2026 margin recovery persists. Mature EBIT ~7.4% vs 6.4% FY2024 peak.

bear.rationale: September's rebound proves a low base: domestic share keeps eroding to Geely/Xiaomi/Leapmotor/Huawei-backed brands, the EU extends anti-subsidy duties to PHEVs, Hungary slips again, and RMB strength keeps eating export margins. Overcapacity holds mature EBIT ~3.9%, with capex staying above D&A and working-capital float unwinding.

scenario_narratives.base: Overseas becomes the growth engine while China stabilises at a lower share: FY2026 revenue roughly flat at ~RMB 800bn (H1 -7%, H2 recovering on the strongest overseas months on record), then +8%/yr for two years as overseas deliveries move from 1.9-2.0m toward the >2.5m FY2027 target, decelerating to 3%. EBIT recovers to ~5.3% in FY2026 from 4.6% (Q2 2026 net margin 4.2% vs 2.7% in Q1) and matures near 5.9%, below the FY2024 6.4% peak because the domestic price war does not fully end and the VAT super-deduction lapses. Capex falls from 19.5% of revenue (FY2025) to 8.5% as the overseas plant and charging build completes, turning owner FCF positive from FY2026 and to a ~4.2% mature margin, just under BYD's best-ever 4.6%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Overseas over-delivers and the Q2 2026 margin trough holds as the low: Hungary reaches series production in Q4 2026, neutralising EU BEV tariffs, overseas units clear 2.5m in FY2027, premium brands (Denza/FANGCHENGBAO/Yangwang) keep compounding and BESS stays global #1. Revenue grows 10-12% for three years and EBITDA holds ~16% before easing to 15.5% (mature EBIT ~7.4%). Working-capital float is partly rebuilt.
scenario_narratives.bear: The domestic price war and EU trade policy both bite: domestic sales keep falling against Geely, Xiaomi, Leapmotor and Huawei-backed brands, the EU extends anti-subsidy duties to the PHEVs BYD has used to route around BEV tariffs, Hungary slips again, and a strong RMB keeps generating FX losses on export receivables. FY2026 revenue falls 4% and growth never exceeds 3%; EBITDA compresses to 12.5% (mature EBIT ~3.9%), capex stays above D&A, and the supplier-payment pledge drains working capital. Owner FCF stays positive but thin (~2.5% mature margin) -- not a solvency case, but the overcapacity case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Held at the prior 25/50/25 (unchanged judgment). Bear 25% (above the 15% house default) because domestic volumes are still down ~33% YTD, EU PHEV tariff extension is live, and the Q2 recovery is one quarter old. Base 50%: H1 2026 margins and the September volume print are consistent with it. Bull 25% (below the 35% default) because it needs Hungary on time, the EU not to extend duties, and the domestic price war to ease -- several independent things going right. Evidence that would move them: two more quarters of Q2-level margins (bull up), or an EU PHEV duty decision / another Hungary delay (bear up).
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is ~0.15% of revenue, so house and street nearly coincide (weighted HKD 61.62 vs 64.19). The price sits above BOTH, so band_position prints far above 100%: it means the market is paying more than even the SBC-as-non-cash value, not that SBC treatment explains the gap. Treat the band as near-collapsed (SBC-light market).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Component owner-FCF DCF in CNY at a single 10% CNY WACC over 10 years, converted to HKD at the observed CNY/HKD rate. Value turns on two things: how far capex intensity falls from the FY2025 19.5% peak toward D&A, and where EBIT settles once the China price war and the overseas ramp net out. The bridge treats BYD on the broad net-cash definition (trading financial assets as cash), adds investment assets whose income is outside EBIT, and deducts the perpetual bonds and the BYD Electronic minority at market. Lead with the base case: the scenario tails are wide and the weighted mean sits close to it only because the weights are symmetric.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex not falling: every 1pp of revenue in sustained capex is ~RMB 8-10bn/yr of owner FCF, roughly HKD 10/share of value at a 12x terminal cap.
EBIT margin: the base needs ~5.9% mature EBIT; FY2025 was 4.6% and the price war is not over.
FX: the RMB has appreciated ~7% vs HKD since July 2026; it raises the HKD value of RMB flows but compresses export margins and creates finance-line losses outside this model's EBIT.
EU trade policy: a PHEV duty extension plus further Hungary delay would hit the highest-margin growth market.
Working capital: BYD's negative working capital (supplier float) is being unwound under the 60-day payment pledge; a faster unwind is a direct cash outflow the base does not model.
Bridge items: trading financial assets (RMB 69.9bn) are treated as cash; if they are less liquid than disclosed, net debt is RMB ~62bn, ~HKD 8/share lower.
